title: Lemma 10.6: locality and strict Henselianity under a surjection
statement_scope: Let φ:A→B be a map of connective E∞-rings which induces a surjection π0A→π0B, and assume B is nonzero. If A is local (respectively strictly Henselian), then B is local (respectively strictly Henselian). Moreover, if R is any local E∞-ring, then a map ψ:B→R is local if and only if the composite ψ∘φ is local; in particular φ is local. Complete statement and proof retained.
